subject: CloudPulse onboarding: DPA / SCCs exception routes and order-form redlines
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@cloudpulse.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudPulse onboarding: DPA / SCCs exception routes and order-form redlines

Sam — thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, attaching our current order form redline and a preliminary DPA/TIA matrix so we can align on a path forward before Legal takes the final pass. High level asks from our side: 

- Confirm whether CloudPulse can accept Redwood as "processor" for the module where we host embeddings, and confirm any controller-to-controller carveouts you expect.
- Clarify the subprocessor list cadence (you had mentioned monthly updates vs quarterly) — we need written cadence for the Order Form exhibit.
- SCCs: your team flagged paragraph on onward transfers. For EU exports to US/UK we will require the standard Clause 14 equivalence flow (or SCCs replacement language). If you need an export carveout for non-standard territories, list them explicitly so we can evaluate the Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) path.

Attached: CP_OrderForm_v1.3_redline.pdf (highlights in-line), DPA_TIA_Matrix_aug18.xlsx (draft mapping of risky jurisdictions).

Proposed next steps:
1) CloudPulse to mark any non-starters in your redline and add commentary in docx (we can accept tracked changes).
2) Redwood Legal (Laura) to triage responses and propose one of: standard SCCs + controller/processor appendix, TIA addendum, or a narrowly scoped export exception.
3) If an exception is requested, route to Exec (Aditya/Finance) for commercial offset (we may need surcharge or SLA change).

Can you aim to return CloudPulse redlines by COB Wed 8/19? Happy to jump on a short call if anything is unclear.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Partnerships — Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: CP_OrderForm_v1.3_redline.pdf (pdf), DPA_TIA_Matrix_aug18.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@cloudpulse.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@cloudpulse.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:47:00 +0100
Subject: Re: CloudPulse onboarding: DPA / SCCs exception routes and order-form redlines

Diego — thanks for sending. I looped in our legal team (legal@cloudpulse.com) and we put initial comments directly into a Word redline (attached). Quick notes up front: 

- Controller/processor: CloudPulse considers itself controller for customer data in our analytics product; for the embedding-hosting module we accept processor designation but need a defined "data scope" exhibit clarifying which data types qualify.
- Subprocessors: we can commit to monthly cadence for notifying changes, but not to pre-approval. We propose a notification + 10 business day objection window in the Order Form.
- Exports: we can accept the standard SCCs (EU Commission clauses) but CloudPulse has a partner in APAC that performs enrichment; if that processing involves personal data we will need a narrowly scoped export carveout for SG/HK — otherwise we will restrict.

I'm attaching: CloudPulse_redlines.docx (tracked changes) and a short note from our counsel on the APAC carveout.

Questions for Redwood Legal: please advise if a 10-business-day objection window for subprocessors is acceptable, and whether an APAC carveout for specific enrichment partners can be handled via a TIA + narrow exhibit instead of a blanket exception.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Lee
Head of Partnerships, CloudPulse Inc.
---
Attachments: CloudPulse_redlines.docx (docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@cloudpulse.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudPulse onboarding: DPA / SCCs exception routes and order-form redlines

Sam / Diego — Laura from Legal here. Thanks for the clear redline, Sam — I reviewed the doc and left inline comments on three items we need to resolve before sign: 

1) Subprocessor cadence & objection window — Redwood typically offers notification + 10 business days for objections on critical subprocessor additions and monthly updates for the roster. We will accept "notification + 10 business days" as proposed but need an explicit definition of "critical" (proposed language below).

2) Controller vs Processor scope — acceptable to treat embedding-hosting as processor provided the Order Form includes a "Data Scope Exhibit" with examples and a short list of excluded controllers (e.g., aggregated benchmarking datasets that CloudPulse controls). I added a draft Exhibit A language in the Word file.

3) APAC enrichment partner carveout — we can handle non-standard territories via a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) plus a named-exception exhibit limited to specific corporate entities (not whole territories). This is preferable to a blanket carveout. If CloudPulse provides the partner legal entity names and typical processing flows (encryption at rest, access controls), we will craft the TIA and attach as an exhibit. 

Operational asks / cost implication note: any TIA that permits transfers outside EU standard equivalence zones may trigger an elevated support SLA and a cross-border handling surcharge. Please confirm if CloudPulse expects reimbursement or prefers reduced SLA (we will route this to Finance for approval).

Proposed timeline: Sam returns partner entity names + redline acceptance on subprocessor objection window by COB Wed 8/19; Redwood Legal will produce a TIA template and Data Scope Exhibit by Fri 8/21. If CloudPulse needs sign-off earlier, propose a focused 30-minute slot tomorrow (Wed) at 10:00 AM CET.

Diego — please escalate to Aditya if CloudPulse requests any commercial offset. Karthik — please prepare a short procurement note on how a surcharge would be surfaced on the order form.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: (inline comments in CloudPulse_redlines.docx)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@cloudpulse.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudPulse onboarding: DPA / SCCs exception routes and order-form redlines

Thanks all — Sam, appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll get the partner entity list to Laura first thing tomorrow and confirm whether CloudPulse expects compensation for the APAC carveout. Karthik, I'll flag Finance and include a one-line ask in the procurement note for an estimated surcharge band.

I think we're aligned on the main path: notification + 10bd objection window; Data Scope Exhibit for processor module; TIA + named-exception exhibit for any APAC partners. If that changes I'll escalate to Aditya/Finance.

Sam — would you prefer we run the TIA draft via the shared Drive link or send a redline via DocuSign envelope when ready?

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Partnerships — Redwood Inference
